questions.title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
questions.background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Resolution Date : Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Michigan's August 4 three-way Democratic Senate primary is essentially a toss-up between U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens and progressive Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, with State Sen. Mallory McMorrow trailing as a live dark horse. Polling averages through early June gave El-Sayed a slight 1.4-3.7 point lead (270toWin: El-Sayed 29.5%, Stevens 26.5%, McMorrow 15.0%), helped by Bernie Sanders' backing and Stevens/McMorrow splitting the moderate Oakland County lane; however, non-partisan Michigan pollsters Glengariff (+2) and late-May TIPP (+4) showed Stevens leading, El-Sayed led only 34-31 in his own Lake Research internal, and Stevens leads heavily among older (65+) and Black primary voters while an AIPAC-linked super PAC just poured nearly $8 million into June ads for her (vs ~$6M reserved by McMorrow's super PAC). With 15-30% undecided and major paid-media battles now unfolding, Stevens and El-Sayed are virtually tied with McMorrow retaining ~14% upset upside.

questions.title: Who will win the Most Valuable Player award at the 2026 MLB All-Star Game?
questions.background: The MLB All-Star Game is an annual exhibition between the American League and National League. Its Most Valuable Player award recognizes an individual player's performance in the game.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : MLB's official announcement of the 2026 All-Star Game MVP, corroborated by contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Timing : The question resolves when the MVP recipient is publicly announced following the 2026 All-Star Game, expected in July 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the player awarded the game's MVP honor.
questions.current_reasoning: The 2026 MLB All-Star Game is July 14 at hitter-friendly Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, and as a single-game exhibition featuring ~60 players, even the top MVP favorites carry only 4%-7% true probability (leaving ~73% on the rest of the field). As of the June 22 Phase 1 voting update, Shohei Ohtani leads all of MLB (2.31M votes) as a locked-in NL DH starter with strong voter bias, while Yordan Alvarez (1.97M votes, 25 HRs, 191 OPS+) and Bobby Witt Jr. (1.70M votes) are runaway AL starting locks. MLB home run leader Kyle Schwarber (29 HRs, Phillies hometown crowd favorite despite minor June 23 back tightness and likely reserve role behind Ohtani) and resurgent two-time ASG MVP Mike Trout (1.74M votes, Philadelphia-area native) round out the top five ahead of Aaron Judge, who has been dealing with a June injury.

local_articles.title: 5 Dodgers, including Ohtani and Freeman named to All-Star Game; Angels' Mike Trout selected for 12th time
local_articles.snippet: As the United States celebrated 250 years on Saturday, the 2026 Major League Baseball All-Star Game starters were announced, with five Los Angeles Dodgers, including superstar Shohei Ohtani, and the Los Angeles Angels' Mike Trout earning spots in the Midsummer Classic. Ohtani, who received the most votes amongst all MLB players, was an automatic selection as a starter. It's his sixth All-Star selection and third as a Dodger. He'll be joined by teammates Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Andy Pages and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. It's Freeman's 10th All-Star selection, Muncy's third, Yamamoto's second and a first for Pages. Each has been instrumental in the Dodgers' double-digit lead over their National League West opponents as they seek their third consecutive World Series championship. questions.title: Which NBA team will LeBron James choose for the 2026–27 season?
questions.background: This question concerns James's publicly announced team choice for the upcoming NBA season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : James's public announcement of his team choice for the 2026–27 season during the 2026 offseason, corroborated by reputable news or sports reporting. Resolution Date : Resolve when James publicly announces that choice. A completed contract signing or appearance in a game is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the NBA team he chooses.
questions.current_reasoning: Late July 3 and July 4 reporting (HoopsHype citing Shams Charania at 11:58 PM ET, Sports Review News citing updated Kalshi pricing, NBC Sports, SI/Yossi Gozlan, Ballislife/DraftKings) drives a sharp repricing between Philadelphia and Golden State. First, Shams Charania formally narrowed LeBron James's decision to six teams: Cavaliers, Heat, Nuggets, Sixers, Timberwolves, and Warriors, while reiterating the choice 'will not be a financially driven money decision'—undercutting Golden State's $15M NTMLE edge. Second, Kalshi repriced sharply by July 3 close (reported July 4): Cleveland 46%, Philadelphia surging to 19% (overtaking GSW!), Golden State sliding 10 points to 17%, Miami 10%, and all others <=4%, while earlier-July-3 DraftKings odds (-115 Cavs, +180 Warriors, +900 Heat, +1000 Sixers, +1200 Nuggets) lagged the podcast fallout. Third, cap analyst Yossi Gozlan revealed Philadelphia has a pathway to offer $6.7M (Dean Wade sign-and-trade plus swapping two non-guaranteed deals)—potentially the largest salary among Rich Paul's five inner-circle teams—while NBC Sports highlighted that Golden State looked like the long shot on Paul's whiteboard and Denver remains stalled on Peyton Watson's RFA. Blending updated Kalshi, DraftKings, and reporting: Cleveland edges up to 0.45 (+0.01), Golden State drops to 0.19 (-0.05), Philadelphia jumps to 0.16 (+0.06), Miami trims to 0.11 (-0.02), and Denver holds 0.045, leaving 4.5% mainly for Minnesota (~3.5%) and any surprise outside the final six.

questions.title: Which ownership group will receive NFL owners' approval to buy the Seattle Seahawks in 2026?
questions.background: The Seattle Seahawks are owned by Paul Allen's estate. Allen's will calls for the team to be sold and the assets distributed to charities.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official NFL announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the purchasing group approved by NFL owners. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the purchasing ownership group in the first sale of the Seattle Seahawks formally approved by NFL owners during 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the purchasing group or the family leading it.
questions.current_reasoning: June 29 Seattle Times coverage citing Bloomberg News reports that first-round bids to buy the Seattle Seahawks were due Monday, June 29 (earlier than previously rumored July 6), that no new potential buyers have emerged beyond the three previously identified groups (Aditya Mittal & Wyc Grousbeck, Todd Boehly, and Vinod Khosla), and that the bidder pool is 'fairly shallow' and 'shrinking' as the record $9B-$10B valuation tests billionaires' cash appetite. Confirming a shallow pool with no newly reported suitors on bid-deadline day concentrates probability mass onto the three active groups (Mittal/Grousbeck 0.30, Boehly 0.25, Khosla 0.23; combined 0.78, up from 0.66), while trimming unmentioned names Apostolopoulos (0.04), Bezos (0.03), and the unannounced mystery-bidder tail (from 23% to 15%).

questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: June 29-July 1 reporting reshapes the Hormuz mine-clearance landscape: after French President Macron met Oman's Sultan Haitham in Paris on June 29 and announced France and Oman would work jointly with partners on demining, Iran angrily rejected foreign/European involvement on June 29-30 (Deputy FM Gharibabadi warning France against 'provocations'; FM spokesman Baqaei insisting demining under Article 5 of the Islamabad MoU is exclusively Iran's responsibility), and German Defense Minister Pistorius conceded July 1 that Germany does not expect to participate given Iran's refusal to cooperate with European countries. Meanwhile, US-Iran indirect technical talks on Hormuz shipping concluded July 1 in Doha mediated specifically by Qatar and Pakistan, and CBS News reiterated that Iran and Oman issued a bilateral joint statement last week on strait management. Oman's Paris demining alignment with France trims Oman modestly (0.29 -> 0.26, though Tehran aimed its public rebuke at France and Oman remains the sole co-littoral partner), while Tehran's hardened rejection of Western/G7 offers shifts mass toward non-Western partners capable of bilateral cooperation—China (0.23 -> 0.25), Islamabad MoU host and Doha mediator Pakistan (0.16 -> 0.18), and Russia (0.13 -> 0.14)—and trims Japan (0.04 -> 0.03), leaving 14% tail mass (Qatar, India, Turkey, UAE, US, etc.).

local_articles.title: Iran envoy says friendly nations to get 'special' Strait of Hormuz fee treatment
local_articles.snippet: Iran's ambassador to China insisted Saturday that new fees would be charged to ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz — an idea rejected by Washington — while assuring that "friendly" nations would receive special treatment. The initial deal struck between Iran and the United States to end their war stipulated that commercial ships would transit the strait free of charge for 60 days, but it remains unclear what will be in place after that period. Iranian Ambassador Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli told the World Peace Forum in Beijing that his country was working in "collaboration and cooperation" with Oman on "new arrangements" for the vital waterway. "As a country where the Hormuz is part of its territorial waters, we will definitely charge service fees," Azli said in translated remarks, while insisting such fees would not be a "toll."
